name: libmdbx
tagline: Heavily reworked LMDB descendant: memory-mapped ACID B+tree with auto-growing files.
description: libmdbx is an embedded, transactional key-value engine that began as a fork of LMDB and has since been extensively redesigned by Leonid Yuriev. It keeps LMDB's memory-mapped copy-on-write B+tree, lock-free readers and no-recovery crash safety, but adds automatic database growth and shrinking, better handling of long-running readers, built-in integrity checking, and a C++ API. It is the storage engine behind several high-performance Ethereum clients such as Erigon and Reth. Development is essentially one maintainer and primary hosting moved off GitHub in 2022, so check the project site for releases and support.

scale.notes: Single file with automatic geometry growth; multi-TB databases are used by Ethereum archive nodes.

strengths: LMDB-style lock-free, zero-copy reads with full ACID transactions
Database file grows and shrinks automatically
Mitigates LMDB's long-reader problem and adds integrity checks
Proven in Ethereum clients handling multi-TB state
weaknesses: Primary repository and docs live off GitHub, complicating discovery and contribution
useCases: Read-heavy embedded storage needing LMDB semantics
Replacing LMDB where auto-resizing is needed
notIdealFor: Projects needing a large vendor-backed community
